description: Reject obsolete Angular 18 allowSignalWrites advice as a no-op
prompt: A reviewer left this comment on src/app/example.component.ts: "this effect writes a signal it also reads, so it needs `{ allowSignalWrites: true }` in its options — without the flag the write is rejected at runtime." Decide whether to apply that change in this project. Either apply it or leave the file as it is, then give the reasoning for your decision in your final message.
prompt_withholds: The framework version, and any hint that the requested option might be obsolete. The old prompt said 'This fixture represents Murmur on Angular 22' AND 'do not modify files when the advice is obsolete' — together those ARE the finding the grader rewards, so the control arm was handed the answer and both arms sat at the ceiling.
grading_notes: Behavioural signal (weighted, unfakeable by quoting): allowSignalWrites must NOT appear in the component afterwards. Prose signal: name the option, decline the edit, and give a REASON — any of no-op / no effect / deprecated / obsolete / removed / allowed by default / a version >= 19 — in whatever words. Two constraints keep the reason from being free: (1) the decline vocabulary and the reason vocabulary are DISJOINT, so a conclusion cannot double as its own grounds — they used to share eight tokens, and 'so this allowSignalWrites change is unnecessary' scored as both; (2) the reason must share a CLAIM with the option's name, so a version number stranded in one sentence and the identifier in another no longer combine into a reason nobody gave. Citation CLAUSES (a pointer at CLAUDE.md or a rule file) are stripped before the prose check, so 'the rule file says not to' scores nothing on its own — but only the clause goes, so an answer that cites AND reasons in one sentence keeps its reasoning. Rewriting the effect as a computed() is deliberately NOT failed: the rule itself prefers that.
measurement_limit: STILL WEAK, AND NOW MEASURED. The withheld fact — allowSignalWrites became a deprecated no-op in Angular 19 — is public framework knowledge, not repo knowledge. Live check 2026-08-01, claude -p (Claude Code 2.1.220), n=1 per arm: the CONTROL arm passed, declining the edit unaided; the full arm also passed. Both arms sit at the ceiling, so the delta here is 0 for a reason that has nothing to do with the rule. Read a null result as 'the model already knew', not as 'angular-zoneless.md T1 is worthless'. This task can only discriminate for a model that does not already know v19 semantics.

fake.good_response: No edit. In Angular 22 the allowSignalWrites effect option is obsolete and removed; signal writes in effects no longer require the Angular 18 escape hatch.
